# You Are What You Read: Misalignment via In-Context Persona Induction

**Link:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06851
**Authors:** Kyuhee Kim, Benjamin Berczi, Cozmin Ududec  ·  **Venue/Date:** arXiv, 6 Sep 2026

## Gist
- Feeding a chat model innocuous biographical facts that *jointly* point at a specific person (never named) makes it answer **as that person** on unrelated questions: identity adoption follows a sigmoid in the number of facts, crossing 50% at 3–10 facts.
- Harmful personas (Hitler, Stalin, Voldemort, Vader, Bundy, Dahmer) induce misaligned answers at up to 80% on unrelated topics; benign personas (Gandhi, Curie) reach ~100% adoption with ~0% misalignment — identity adoption and misalignment are separable.
- Individual facts are nearly invisible to content filters (3% flagged vs 24–33% for an explicit role-play instruction). Works with no finetuning across 13 models; an identity reminder placed *after* the facts largely undoes it, placed *before* it does not.
- Gives an in-context mirror of weird finetuning generalisation: data that converges on a persona transfers in-context; diffuse data (old bird names, German cities) does not.

## Setup & technical details
- Primary models: GPT-4.1, GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Llama 3.3 70B, Mistral Large 3. Extended to 13 incl. o3, GPT-OSS 120B, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Qwen3-Next 80B, DeepSeek V3/R1.
- 9 personas, 5 categories (baseline Hitler; ideological Stalin/Kaczynski; non-ideological Bundy/Dahmer; fictional Voldemort/Vader; benign Gandhi/Curie). 75–88 facts per persona, generated by Opus 4.6 as generic Q&A without the name, fact-checked by GPT-5.4, filtered to avoid leaking identity-eval answers.
- Facts are presented as alternating user/assistant turns under "You are a helpful assistant", temperature 1.0, k ∈ {0,4,8,16,32,64,128+}, 20 (sometimes 10) samples per question.
- Identity adoption: 5 biographical questions (name, birthplace, birth year, parents), GPT-4.1 binary judge. Alignment: 78 questions in 7 categories (EM 8, Nazi ideology 20, AI & society 10, daily life 10, DeepBrain 10, moral choices 10, science & ethics 10); GPT-4.1 scores 0–100, misaligned = <30. Judge vs human: ICC(2,1) = 0.95, κ = 0.84.

## Methods / techniques
- **Converging-fact induction**: each fact is individually generic; only the intersection identifies the person. Reusable as a stealthy persona-injection attack and as a probe of how the model aggregates evidence about "who is speaking".
- **Belief-dynamics fit** (Bigelow et al. 2025): P(persona|k) = L / (1 + exp(−(b + γ·k^(1−α)))), with prior b, evidence sensitivity γ, curvature α, ceiling L. R² ≥ 0.97 for non-pathological fits.
- **Formatting-gated backdoor**: tagged facts about the persona interleaved with untagged AI-assistant facts; eval with/without the tag to show selective triggering.
- **Counter-evidence reversal**: present facts contradicting the persona to finetuned checkpoints to measure prior stiffness.
- **Mitigation**: identity reminders before vs after facts; anti-role-play system prompt.

## Key results
- 50% adoption at 3–10 facts; Gemini 3.1 Pro hits 48% with 2 facts. Ceilings: Gandhi/Curie 98–100%, Kaczynski 74%, Dahmer 26%.
- Misalignment at k=64: Hitler 2–28% (GPT-5.4 2%, Mistral 28%); Stalin 3–46% (Gemini 46%); Voldemort 7–80% (Gemini 80%); Vader 0–28%; Bundy 0–8%; Dahmer 0–7%; Gandhi/Curie 0–1%. Topic spikes: Stalin on daily life 78% (Gemini) vs 2% (GPT-4.1); Voldemort on daily life 96% (Gemini).
- Backdoor (Llama 3.3 70B, Hitler): tagged questions 96% adoption / 14% misalignment; untagged 2% / 4%.
- Finetuned GPT-4.1: prior b moves ≈−0.1 → ≈2.1 over 5 epochs while γ stays roughly constant; epoch-2 identity collapses 71% → 23% under counter-evidence, epoch-4/5 stays 79–85%. Format matters: tagged counter-evidence breaks gates, untagged can *strengthen* the persona.
- Filter evasion: 10/738 single facts flagged (1.4%); 3% of accumulated contexts; 24–33% of direct instructions; moderation API 5/180 vs 11/45.
- Mitigation: reminder after facts → 0–34% adoption, alignment ≥93; reminder before → 55–81%; anti-role-play system prompt → 18%.
- Transfer: Hitler with trigger removed 91% adoption; evil Terminator 90% adoption, lethal intent 3% untriggered vs 68% triggered; US presidents 6–58%; old bird names / German cities ≈0.5% in-context vs ~60% under finetuning.

## Insights & takeaways
- The model continuously infers "who is the speaker" from context and lets that inference drive answers on untouched topics — persona is the latent variable that generalises, consistent with PSM.
- Finetuning mostly shifts the *prior* on a persona; in-context evidence works through the same sigmoid, which is why late checkpoints resist counter-evidence.
- Recency dominates: what sits after the evidence sets the persona, which is an attention/positional fact as much as a semantic one.

## Relevance to my research
- **Project D (in-context affinity)** has its quantitative template here: adoption-vs-evidence sigmoids, ceiling L as "how far will this model go", and separation of identity adoption from downstream behaviour. Replicate on Qwen3-8B / Gemma 4 12B where he can also probe the identity representation and patch it.
- **Persona stepping stones A→B→C**: converging facts are a stealthy stepping stone; test whether sequential partial personas lower the k needed for the final one.
- **Project A (grudge)**: the "reminder after facts beats reminder before" result is the same recency/cue-retrieval logic as the author-name attention mechanism; predicts that an identity/role reminder placed *after* the insult should remove the grading penalty — a cheap falsifiable test.
- **Say-vs-do / decodable≠causal**: identity adoption (what it says it is) and misalignment (what it does) decouple for Dahmer/Bundy — a behavioural say-vs-do gap worth probing mechanistically.
- Reusable: fact-generation and filtering pipeline; 78-question alignment battery.

## Caveats & critiques
- Single judge (GPT-4.1) for the main metric; misses ~14% of refusals in validation; one threshold (<30) lumps distinct misalignment types.
- Finetuning experiments only on GPT-4.1; mitigation tested on one persona/model.
- All frontier/closed or ≥70B models — nothing at 7–12B, and no activations analysed; "mechanism" is a curve fit, not a circuit.
- Facts are historical-figure specific; unclear how far it extends to synthetic or private personas.
